item.title: Gangoji: The Ancient Temple Within Naramachi — Guide
item.description: Gangoji is one of Nara’s quietest World Heritage treasures, tucked into the lanes of Naramachi — the merchant quarter that in fact grew up within this once-vast temple’s former grounds. Gangoji traces its origins to Asuka-dera, Japan’s very first full-scale Buddhist temple founded in 588, and when the capital moved to Nara the temple moved with it. Though far smaller today, its main hall (Gokurakubo) is a National Treasure, and remarkably some of its roof still bears original tiles from the Asuka period, over 1,400 years old — among the oldest roofing in the world — making a modest visit a brush with the very dawn of Japanese Buddhism.
